newsitem.title: UK: UK tabloids droole over Di's new love affair.
newsitem.headline: UK tabloids droole over Di's new love affair.

text.p: Britain's royalty-obsessed tabloid newspapers drooled over Princess Diana's apparent new romance with millionaire film producer Dodi Fayed on Monday and declared the couple a perfect love match.

Diana's relationship with the 41-year-old son of controversial Harrods department store boss Mohammed Al Fayed may be just a few weeks old, but newspapers confidently predicted a wedding and compared the match to Jackie Kennedy's marriage to Aristotle Onassis.
Papers declared that, like Jackie Onassis, Diana needs a wealthy husband who can provide her with the high life she craves while sheltering her from the media clamour that follows her every move.
Dodi, a veteran of the international jet set, could offer the fashion-loving Princess that and much more.
"Glamorous, passionate, attention-seeking: they are made for each other," Lynda Lee-Potter wrote in the Daily Mail of the reported love match.
Dodi Fayed has previously dated a string of film stars including Brooke Shields, "so he's used to highly-strung, tricky women," declared Lee-Potter.
His good relationship with his "overbearing" father "must mean that he is tactful, non-confrontational and emollient, albeit a little weak," Lee-Potter added.
In short, he is nothing like Britain's heir to the throne Prince Charles, from whom Diana was divorced last year after a blighted 15-year marriage.
Unlike Charles, Dodi Fayed would not resent Diana's passion for the limelight, and her ability to claim it, and he appears to be genuinely in love with her, Lee-Potter said.
For Dodi Fayed, Diana offered not only her famed good looks, but an opportunity to cock a snook at the British establishment which has long spurned his family.

Mohammed Al Fayed, one of the richest men in the world, has had homes in Britain for 30 years but his requests for a British passport were repeatedly turned down by successive Conservative governments.

"If (Dodi) enables Mohammed Al Fayed to introduce Princess Diana as 'my future daughter-in-law' he will have fulfilled his ambitious father's greatest dream, which is to feel an integral part of the British aristocracy," wrote Lee-Potter.

Some papers even speculated that Mohammed Al Fayed planned to give the couple the Paris villa which was home to the Duke and Duchess of Windsor -- the couple who scandalised the royal family in 1936 when the Duke abdicated from the British throne to marry the divorcee he loved.
Al Fayed bought the lease on the Paris villa 15 years ago after the Duchess's death.

The Dodi and Diana story became Britain's hottest media property on Sunday when a tabloid newspaper published a series of hazy photographs showing the couple kissing and embracing while on a Mediterranean cruise together.
Such is the interest in Diana's love life that the Italian photographer who snatched the blurry pictures through a telephoto lens has become a millionaire overnight.

The prospect that the princess had finally found love almost completely overshadowed her trip to Bosnia last week, intended to highlight the plight of landmine victims -- at least as far as the British press was concerned.

Diana, who flew back to Britain late on Sunday, left a country where charities struggle to raise 700 pounds ($1,110) for a pair of artificial limbs. She went back to a world whose media paid 700,000 pounds to buy paparazzi shots," commented the Guardian newspaper.

But it seems the princess was as interested as anyone else to see what the papers were saying about her. As she waited for her plane to take off, reporters spotted her sifting through a pile of Sunday's tabloids. ($ = 0.630 British Pounds)
